dom.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment

st.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment
st.an: The study materially extends the cluster’s case for selective, human-centred deployment by providing real-world, task-level evidence that sustained AI assistance may weaken unaided professional performance through over-reliance. This strengthens the rationale for capability-preservation measures and use-context-specific evaluation, although the evidence is medical rather than legal and the observational design cannot establish causation.
qs: ADR of standard colonoscopy significantly decreased  from 28.4% (226/795) before to 22.4% (145/648) after the exposure to AI, corresponding to a 6%  absolute reduction (95% confidence interval: -10.5% to -1.6%).

kp.k: Study examines unaided performance after AI exposure
kp.d: This medical study examines possible deskilling rather than legal services. The retrospective observational analysis covered four Polish endoscopy centers from 8 September 2021 to 9 March 2022, comparing approximately three months before and after AI implementation. The primary sample comprised 1,443 non-AI-assisted diagnostic colonoscopies: 795 before implementation and 648 afterward. Nineteen trained endoscopists, each with experience of over 2,000 colonoscopies, performed the procedures.
qs: We conducted a retrospective observational study at four endoscopy centers in Poland.
The primary outcome was adenoma detection rate (ADR) of standard, non-AI assisted colonoscopy.
experience of over 2,000 colonoscopies each.

kp.d: The study was nested in the ACCEPT randomized implementation project, with AI activation determined by examination date. Diagnostic patients consequently received procedures with or without assistance after implementation, although the primary before-and-after comparison remained observational. The system was Olympus ENDO-AID CADe. The first 100 colonoscopies per center after implementation were excluded for familiarization; individual endoscopists' exposure during that period could vary. Endoscopists could see AI markings, preventing blinding.
qs: On AI days, the AI processor is automatically activated, while on non-AI days, it is automatically deactivated.
The implemented AI system was ENDO-AID CADe (OIP-1, Olympus Medical Systems Corp., Tokyo)

kp.k: Unaided adenoma detection declined after AI exposure
kp.d: ADR in non-AI-assisted procedures fell from 28.4% (226/795) before implementation to 22.4% (145/648) afterward: a 6.0-percentage-point absolute reduction, with 95% CI −10.5 to −1.6 percentage points and p=0.009. Mixed-effects multivariable logistic regression, including endoscopist as a random effect, reported an adjusted odds ratio of 0.69 (95% CI 0.53–0.89; p=0.004) for post-implementation exposure. The authors interpret this association as suggesting a possible detrimental effect on unaided capability, not definitive causal proof of deskilling.

kp.k: Other measured outcomes showed no significant differences
kp.d: Mean adenomas per colonoscopy fell from 0.54 to 0.43, but the reported difference of 0.11 was not statistically significant (95% CI −0.01 to 0.24; p=0.071). Mean advanced adenomas per colonoscopy remained similar at 0.062 versus 0.063 (p=0.918). Among patients with at least one adenoma, mean adenoma counts were 1.91 before versus 1.92 after exposure (p=0.954). Colorectal cancers were detected in six procedures before exposure and eight afterward (p=0.35). ADR is presented as a quality indicator associated with cancer prevention; the study's central result concerns detection rather than subsequent cancer incidence.

kp.k: Regression table qualifies narrative descriptions of predictors
kp.d: Table 3 identifies male patients versus female patients as having adjusted odds ratio 1.78 (95% CI 1.38–2.30), and patients aged ≥60 versus <60 as having adjusted odds ratio 3.60 (95% CI 2.74–4.72). These reference categories differ from the abstract and narrative descriptions, which attach these estimates to female sex and age <60. The table also reports other indications versus alarm symptoms at adjusted odds ratio 1.36 (95% CI 0.89–2.08; p=0.154), despite the narrative describing alarm symptoms as an independent factor. The table therefore does not establish a statistically significant adjusted association for indication.
qs: All models include endoscopists as a random effect
Variables with a p-value <0.05 in the univariate model were included in the multivariable model.

kp.k: Overreliance is proposed, not directly established
kp.d: The authors hypothesize that reliance on AI recommendations may reduce clinicians' motivation, focus and responsibility when making unaided decisions. They cite psychological research on automation-related skill decay, an experimental colonoscopy study showing reduced visual eye movements with AI, and mammography research reporting diminished detection when AI support was expected. These provide proposed mechanisms and supporting cross-domain context, rather than direct measurements of the psychological cause of this study's ADR decline.

kp.k: AI-exposed controls might exaggerate apparent treatment benefits
kp.d: The authors raise the hypothesis that randomized trials comparing AI-assisted procedures with non-AI-assisted procedures may partly capture deterioration in the latter when the same practitioners have ongoing AI exposure. In this study, post-implementation AI-assisted ADR was 25.3% (186/734), compared with 22.4% without assistance during the same phase and 28.4% before implementation. Supplementary Table 6 reports an adjusted odds ratio of 0.80 (95% CI 0.63–1.02) for assisted procedures versus pre-implementation procedures, not a significant improvement. The authors present control-group contamination as a possible explanation for some prior trial benefits, not an established reinterpretation of all trials.

kp.d: ADR declined across all four centers, with larger reported reductions at centers with higher baseline detection. The authors acknowledge regression to the mean as an alternative explanation. Reported reductions were 2.9 percentage points for male endoscopists and 15.1 for female endoscopists. Patient subgroup declines occurred among women below and above 60 and men below 60, whereas men aged 60 or older showed a 1.6-point increase. Individual endoscopist volumes were insufficient for reliable individual-level conclusions; Figure 2 excluded four practitioners with fewer than ten procedures in either phase. Supplementary Table 1 gives the surgeons' reduction as 8.3 points with CI −18.9 to 2.4, unlike the negative upper bound stated in the narrative.

kp.k: Confounding and workflow changes limit causal inference
kp.d: The authors explicitly caution that the observational design is vulnerable to selection bias and confounding despite stratification and regression adjustment. Patient characteristics and indications differed between phases, with indications unknown for 37.2% overall. Diagnostic procedure volume rose from 795 before implementation to 1,382 afterward, including 734 assisted procedures, following suspension of Poland's colonoscopy screening programme on 1 January 2022. This freed diagnostic capacity and could confound the comparison. Other limitations include one AI system, experienced operators only, no blinding, missing withdrawal-time data, no sample-size calculation and exclusion of sessile serrated lesions from ADR.

kp.k: Prospective research should test skill-preservation measures
kp.d: The authors recommend robust prospective studies, including randomized crossover trials, to test generalizability and behavioral research to investigate mechanisms. They identify explainable AI and cognitive forcing techniques as possible interventions for future investigation, not measures validated by this study. They also call for studies involving less-experienced operators because AI-supported training is an important prospective use. These recommendations concern medical capability; the document does not directly establish effects on lawyers or legal training.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Budzyń and colleagues suggest that regular exposure to AI polyp-detection assistance may reduce endoscopists’ performance when they subsequently work without AI.
pts.d: This is a cross-domain medical source, not a claim about legal services. The authors report a decline in adenoma detection rate (ADR) during non-AI-assisted colonoscopy after AI implementation and interpret it as possible deskilling. They hypothesize that reliance on AI may reduce clinicians’ motivation, focus and responsibility during unaided decisions; these mechanisms were not directly established by the study. They also suggest that AI exposure could depress performance in non-AI control groups in randomized trials, potentially accounting for part of the apparent advantage of AI assistance. Separately, they describe previous randomized evidence of improved detection while AI is actively used and an expected cancer-prevention benefit, rather than claiming this study demonstrated such a benefit.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The principal evidence is a retrospective before-and-after observational comparison, supplemented by adjusted analyses and references to earlier trials and behavioral studies.
pts.d: Across four Polish centers, 1,443 non-AI-assisted colonoscopies were compared: 795 before and 648 after AI implementation. ADR fell from 28.4% to 22.4%, a 6.0-percentage-point decrease (95% CI −10.5 to −1.6; p=0.009). Mixed-effects logistic regression, accounting for endoscopists, reported an adjusted odds ratio of 0.69 (95% CI 0.53–0.89; p=0.004) for post-implementation exposure. Mean adenomas per colonoscopy declined from 0.54 to 0.43 without statistical significance (p=0.071); advanced adenomas per colonoscopy were similar (0.062 versus 0.063; p=0.918). The additional 734 AI-assisted procedures had an ADR of 25.3%; the adjusted comparison with pre-implementation unaided procedures was not statistically significant. The authors support their proposed behavioral mechanism with cited eye-gaze, mammography and nonclinical automation research, not direct measurements of cognitive skill decay in this cohort. Their account of active AI benefits cites a meta-analysis of 20 randomized trials reporting an 8.1-percentage-point ADR increase. Table 3 identifies male sex and age ≥60 as the higher-odds categories, despite reversed category descriptions in the abstract and results prose; the indication variable was not statistically significant after adjustment.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The observed association concerns approximately three months before and after late-2021 AI implementation, with substantial qualifications about causation and generalizability.
pts.d: The study covered September 8, 2021 to March 9, 2022. Following implementation, AI assistance was switched on or off according to examination date within the ACCEPT implementation project; the deskilling analysis itself remained an observational before-and-after comparison. The first 100 post-implementation colonoscopies per center were excluded for familiarization. Only one system, ENDO-AID CADe, was studied. The authors acknowledge selection bias, confounding, absence of blinding, missing withdrawal-time data, limited procedure counts for some operators and possible regression to the mean in higher-baseline centers. Diagnostic procedure volume nearly doubled after implementation following suspension of Poland’s screening program, which they identify as a potential confounder. They do not establish whether the apparent performance change persists, reverses or occurs among less-experienced operators, and call for prospective and behavioral research. Explainable AI and cognitive forcing techniques are proposed research directions, not demonstrated remedies.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The immediate subjects are experienced endoscopists and their diagnostic-colonoscopy patients; the broader concern is preservation of physician capability as medical AI spreads.
pts.d: The cohort involved 19 trained endoscopists—16 physicians and three general surgeons—each with experience of more than 2,000 colonoscopies. Patients may be affected through reduced detection of precancerous lesions during unaided procedures. ADR is associated with cancer prevention, but the study did not establish increased subsequent cancer incidence or mortality. The authors describe potentially larger declines among female endoscopists, female patients and centers with higher baseline ADR, while cautioning that subgroup findings need further research and that operator-level numbers were insufficient for reliable assessment. Findings cannot directly establish effects on trainees or on professionals in other domains, including lawyers.
